text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The newspaper publishes parts from the book titled "Conspiracies of international policies" by Athanassios Strigas who claims Berisha received $10 million from the West to get Albania under its control.
- June elections will be monitored by some 800 observers from the OSCE, United States, Britain, and Ireland. Multinational forces will be present during the voting.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino insists the state of emergency should be lifted before the elections.
- Italian and Turkish troops of the multinational forces have asked to hold a friendly soccer match with Tirana club.
- Hospital staff in the south say they have enough medicaments, but have to suffer threats from armed men.
- Two arm depots with spare parts for tanks in Elbasan, central Albania, were burnt on Wednesday night.
- Two masked and armed people looted some 50 million leks at the savings bank in Berat, 120 km south of Tirana.
- The Union for Democracy alliance of the Democratic party with four other small parties will hold a rally in Tirana in the afternoon.
- Police have put the capital Tirana under tight control after some explosions and scores of telephone calls threatening bomb attacks.
- Maria Marshall, 50, a French woman who received Albanian citizenship a year ago, will run as an independent candidate in the western town of Kavaje.
- OSCE opens its office in the southern town of Gjirokaster.
- President Berisha has still not signed the decree for the law on the transparency of pyramid investment schemes.
- The Socialist party nominated candidates for the June 29 elections.
